properties.areaDesc: Northern Denali Borough; Southern Denali Borough
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 19 at 8:48PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 5 and 10
inches. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Denali Borough.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Tuesday to 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...North and west of Healy, the chance for heavy
snow drops off quickly due to a narrow gradient of snow. There is
potential for greater than 6 inches in Healy but only a few inches
in Anderson. The exact placement of the area of heavier will have a
dramatic effect on the final snowfall totals. If the band moves a
few dozen miles west, snowfall totals will be on the higher end of
the range, especially near Healy. If the band moves a few dozen
miles east, snowfall totals will likely be on the lower end, even
in Healy.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Fortymile Country; Upper Tanana Valley; Delta Junction
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 19 at 8:48PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:

inches expected, with 1 to 3 inches expected from Northway to the
Alcan Border along the Alaska Highway. Locally higher snow totals
of 12 to 16 inches will be possible, especially between Tanacross
and Dot Lake. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph. Rain may mix with
snow in the Upper Tanana Valley around Northway to the Alcan
Border.

* WHERE...Delta Junction, Fortymile Country, and Upper Tanana Valley.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Northwest wind gusts may be as high as 35 mph
Tuesday morning through early Wednesday morning.
properties.instruction:

clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.description:

inches.

* WHERE...Fairbanks, Fox, Chatanika, Ester and Nenena.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow

location of this heavier snow area. This detail will be crucial in
determining which spots get 6 inches or more versus 3 inches or

differences. If the area of heavier snow shifts slightly west,
heavy snow becomes more likely over the area. If the area of
heavier snow shifts slightly east, heavy snow becomes less likely
over the area.

inches expected. Wind could gust as high as 35 mph across higher
elevations.

* WHERE...Upper Chena River Valley, Southern and Eastern Yukon Flats,
White Mountains, and Eagle Summit.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Gusty winds could lead to

quickly. Locations near Beaver and Livengood may end up getting
closer to 2 to 4 inches or less.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 19 at 9:47PM AST until October 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to
12 feet. For the HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, life-threatening rip
currents.

* WHERE...For the HIGH SURF ADVISORY and HIGH RIP CURRENT, the
most vulnerable areas are the exposed northwesterly and north-
facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory remains from 2 AM to 6 PM AST
Tuesday. For the High Rip Current Risk remains from 2 AM AST
Tuesday through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...FOR THE HIGH SURF ADVISORY, High waves that can wash
over jetties and sweep people and pets onto jagged rocks.
Rough surf may also knock you down. Large breaking waves will
result in localized beach/dune structure erosion and dangerous
swimming conditions. FOR THE HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 19 at 3:22PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river, currently over the Yakutat area, is expected
to continue through Tuesday. Multiple periods of heavy rain are
expected for the Icy Strait corridor and northeast Gulf Coast,
including the following communities: Yakutat, Elfin Cove, Pelican,
Gustavus, Juneau. Elevated gusty winds are expected alongside this
heavier rainfall, with the strongest winds from the southwest
expected late Tuesday morning into Tuesday afternoon. Prolonged
periods of moderate to heavy rain will produce significant river
rises with the potential for at least minor flooding in Juneau and
Gustavus. Ponding of water in low-lying areas is also possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Northeast Gulf Coast and Northern
Inner Channels. This includes the cities of Yakutat, Gustavus, And
Juneau.

* WHEN...From 10 PM AKDT this evening through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals for the Yakutat area between this morning and Tuesday
evening range between 4.5-7.0 inches, with greater than 9 inches
possible at elevations greater than 1000 ft. For Gustavus, rain
totals ranging between 2-4 inches, exceeding 4 inches on south to
southwest facing mountains along the outer coast, and exceeding 4
inches on south to southwest facing mountains at elevation in
Glacier Bay and around Gustavus.

For the Juneau area, rain totals have trended slightly down,
ranging between 2 and 3 inches with totals exceeding 4 inches at
elevations greater than 4 inches. Highest rain rates are expected
overnight tonight into Tuesday with rain rates as high as 0.2
inches per hour.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
